pairs.difference: A: dark, doubled contour along the roof, gold trim, fenders and bumper, plus packed lines in the grille and wheel spokes. Subject density 0.317 is above the real range. B: plank gaps on the dock are thick and black and the water has many ripple rings, but its subject density of 0.14 is in range and the boat hull contour thins out.
pairs.fix: Drop the dark line around the roof and fenders. Let the body meet the background through a change of color only. Simplify the grille to a few broad bars and the wheels to fewer spokes. Keep the panel seams hair-thin.

pairs.difference: B: the jack-o'-lantern's eyes, nose and mouth are ringed by a heavy, even, doubled line, the handle has a continuous wire contour and the candy wrappers are busy. Outline darkness of 0.098 sits at the top of the real range. A: ball seams are thin and taper off, and the upper-left silhouette nearly disappears, like a real card's soft edges. A's low density of 0.029 comes from a simple object, so it says little. Sand speckle is its only noisy area.
pairs.fix: Remove the dark rim around the carved face. Show the cutouts as soft inner shading that fades at the edges. Let the pumpkin's rib grooves stay faint. Thin the handle's edge and allow parts of it to fade into the background.

pairs.difference: A: the coastlines are thick, doubled, wobbly lines, and the map border, compass and water marks are all drawn with the same heavy weight. Background density of 0.077 is above the real range, and subject density of 0.18 is at its ceiling. B is the sailor cap from the real set: a thin rim on the crown, lost edges along the crown's right side and soft cap folds, with the crispest edge at the badge.
pairs.fix: Paint the continents as flat color shapes with no line along the coast. Use one thin map border. Keep the sharpest edge only on the magnifier rim. Calm the floor by removing most wood-grain lines and board-gap lines.

pairs.difference: A: a heavy dark contour runs around the lid, the straps and every plank, with dense wood-grain lines, ring-shaped rivets, and cracked flagstones drawn as lines in the floor. Edges are spread evenly over hero and ground. B: density of 0.086 is at the low end, with soft edges on the ice cubes and tray walls. Its busy parts are only the frost speckle and the table's dark board gaps.
pairs.fix: Remove the dark line around the chest and straps. Reduce wood grain to a few faint marks. Use thin plank seams instead of grooves. Make the stone floor soft patches of tone without drawn cracks.

pairs.difference: A: each sticker shape on the cover is ringed by a thick, doubled contour, and the bookmark tabs and cover edge carry hard bands too. Outline darkness of 0.165 is the only value above the real range in this pair. B: the corners, spine bands and star have strong but fitted edges, the stitching is thin and neat, and the cover interior stays quiet, within the real outline range.
pairs.fix: Make the cover pictures flat printed color with no raised rim or double line around them. Soften the shapes' edges. Keep the cover's corners crisp with a thin highlight, not a dark band.

pairs.difference: A: several concentric hard rings run around the flask, with an extra bright rim and glow outside the dark line, and more hard rings on bubbles, neck and cork. Outline darkness of -0.133 is outside the real range. B: one thin outer edge, with lost edges inside the bottle's translucent body and only the curved groove marked.
pairs.fix: Draw the flask's edge as one thin glass rim with no glowing ring around it. Let the lower glass fade softly into the liquid. Give the bubbles soft edges and use fewer hard rings. Remove the halo against the background.

pairs.difference: B: heavy dark contours on the shoe sole and side panels, dense laces and a fine mesh grid, with subject density of 0.227 at the real ceiling. Outline darkness of -0.1 is outside the real range, and the wall-floor line is hard and ruler-straight. A: skull edges are soft and broad, with thin lines only at the teeth and eye sockets and a lost edge on the left of the cranium. Density is low because the form is simple.
pairs.fix: Remove the dark line around the soles and panels. Replace the mesh grid with smooth tone and only a hint of texture. Reduce the laces to a few simple thick cords. Blend the wall-floor join softly.

pairs.difference: B: a continuous dark line follows the whole bat silhouette, both wings and the ears, and it is the same weight around the wing scallops. Outline darkness of -0.118 is outside the real range. A: the wristband's outer contour is faint and partly lost on the top and right, with its sharper edges concentrated on the raised music icons, which gives a clear edge hierarchy.
pairs.fix: Remove the dark line around the wings and ears. Let the purple wing edge meet the yellow background directly with a clean color change. Keep the sharpest detail on the face and let the wing tips soften.

pairs.difference: B: the web tubes are double-walled, with dark lines on both sides of every strand and hard rings at the joints, so the hero is covered in similar edges with no focus. Subject density of 0.271 is well above the real range. A: the whistle has a thin, even contour and empty interior, with density of 0.039 slightly below the real range. The web's density is partly due to its subject, so this call is weak.
pairs.fix: Make the web strands softer, with no dark lines along their sides. Use fewer rings of web and thinner connecting threads. Leave only the center and droplet crisp, and let outer strands fade slightly.

pairs.difference: B: every leaf on the topiary has its own dark edge, and the background hedge and paving are also noisy, so hero and ground compete. Subject density of 0.29 is above the real range and background density is 0.037. A: the trunk has streaky hair-like bark lines and a strong contour on the branches, with outline darkness of -0.099 just outside range, but density of 0.153 is in range and the sky and hills stay quiet.
pairs.fix: Group the leaves into a few big clumps with soft tone changes. Draw individual leaves only near the lit center of each tier. Turn the background hedge into a soft green mass with no leaf detail. Simplify the paving.

pairs.difference: B: thick dark contours ring every petal and flower center, and the stone border blocks have doubled lines and wide grooves, though its density of 0.137 is in range. A: balloons have soft, thin edges with lost contours against the sky and clouds, and the sharpest mark is on the string bow. A's density of 0.028 is below range only because the balloons are smooth forms.
pairs.fix: Remove the dark line around petals and flower centers. Separate flowers with soft shadow and color instead. Make the gaps between border stones thin and shallow. Keep the sharpest edges on the front flower only.

pairs.difference: A: every ivy leaf has a dark doubled contour and the wreath is packed with lines, and the leaf shadows on the door appear as wobbly bands. Edges fill the frame from corner to corner with no rest area. Subject density of 0.342 and background density of 0.107 are both above the real range. B: castle stones have fairly strong contours and grooves, but all three measures are in range and the sky and grass stay quiet.
pairs.fix: Paint the ivy as soft green masses with only a few clear leaves near the door. Remove the dark line around each leaf. Keep the sharpest edges on the wreath alone. Make door panels thin precise seams and soften the shadows on the door.

pattern: Generated cards draw a heavy, even, continuous contour around the hero and around internal shapes, often as a doubled line, so seams read as grooves and silhouettes never fade out. Edge weight is spread evenly, with no sharp focus and softer periphery, and small parts (leaves, rivets, wood grain, plank gaps, mesh, stickers) each get their own hard ring. Background texture also gets too many edges. Real cards keep seams thin, let parts of the silhouette go soft or lost, and stay quiet away from the focus. Low edge density alone is not a tell, because simple real objects also read low.
